clue.text: Apparatus for divers from South Island

parts.note: Cuba is a Caribbean island

explanation.surface: A piece of diving kit shipped in from somewhere in the South Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: The self-contained underwater breathing apparatus worn by divers goes by this acronym.

clue.text: Policeman's baton damaged a fellow in organization

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A copper's truncheon is broken and a colleague in the force is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the possessive S of 'Policeman's' is part of the fodder: POLICEMANS plus BATON rearranged ('damaged') gives the fifteen letters; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stable companion is literally a horse from the same stable, figuratively a fellow member of the same organization.

clue.text: Internal part of gun, if you make one

indicators.note: an internal part lies inside, so the answer is found within the run of letters of these words

explanation.surface: A gunsmith's remark about a component inside a firearm you might build yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: To unify things is to join them together into a single whole, so it means to make one.

clue.text: Skill needed to catch, in a way, many a tropical insect

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so the skill word holds the next piece within it

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

indicators.note: put in a different way, so the letters of the word many are rearranged

explanation.surface: A naturalist needs some skill to trap the many insects of the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch' reads as trapping the insect, but it tells the skill word to hold the scrambled 'many' ('in a way' gives MYAN); the trailing 'a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Army ants are tropical ants that hunt in huge marching columns.

clue.text: Most of Galsworthy's family greeting a bloomer in spring

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter, so the family name loses its final letter

parts.note: John Galsworthy wrote The Forsyte Saga about the Forsyte family
hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: Galsworthy's clan, mostly, say hello to a flower as the season turns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the last E of FORSYTE, leaving FORSYT.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsythia is a shrub whose bright yellow flowers appear in early spring.

clue.text: Cheese with fine character from Greece

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek cheese with plenty of character.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white brined cheese, typically made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Go over main points with union before communist is taken back

parts.note: to recap is to summarize the main points again
TU is short for trade union
red is a common name for a communist

explanation.surface: A summary to the trade union before a communist is recaptured.
explanation.definitionFit: Recaptured means seized again, so taken back.

clue.text: Source of many a bow, as you said, old actor's taken

indicators.note: said signals that the word you is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: you is said aloud and heard as the name of a tree
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: An archer recalls what you said and how a veteran actor was captured.
explanation.walkthrough: Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a leading London actor-manager around 1900; 'as' and 's taken' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Longbows were traditionally made of yew wood, so the tree is their source.

clue.text: Explosive leading article, remarkably unorthodox

indicators.note: leading means coming first, so the explosive goes in front of the next piece

parts.note: HE stands for high explosive

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something altered out of the ordinary, so the letters of article are rearranged

explanation.surface: A journalist's lead article on explosives is surprisingly unconventional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive leading article' reads as a heated editorial, but 'leading' only puts the explosive first, and 'remarkably' scrambles the article (RETICAL).
explanation.definitionFit: Heretical views depart from accepted doctrine, so they are unorthodox.

clue.text: Government official worked on treaty with military leader

indicators.note: worked suggests being kneaded into shape, so the letters of on and treaty are rearranged

parts.note: a general is a senior army commander

explanation.surface: A minister drafted a treaty together with an army commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges ON and TREATY into ATTORNEY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Attorney General is the government's chief law officer.

clue.text: Man with a little twitch after a vote is taken for granted

indicators.note: after puts the pieces before it later in the answer than the pieces that follow it

parts.note: X is the mark made on a ballot paper as a vote
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man
a tic is a small involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Someone with a nervous tic votes, and the result is assumed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man (IOM), not a person; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something axiomatic is self-evident, accepted without proof.

clue.text: Best German dish — nothing substituted in order?

indicators.note: substituted means one letter is swapped in for another in the sausage word

parts.note: wurst is German sausage
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Praising a fine German sausage, with a query about whether something is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: O replaces the U of WURST; 'in order?' is a whimsical link, since O and U sit next to each other in vowel order.
explanation.definitionFit: To worst someone is to defeat them, the same verb sense as to best them.

clue.text: No cleric was lying to bishop, for example

parts.note: lay is the past tense of lie, so it means was lying
a bishop is one of the pieces, or men, in chess

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone told lies to a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bishop' is a chess piece, a man, not a churchman; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A layman is a member of the laity, someone who is not a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Manipulative type of person speaking about working out

indicators.note: about means around, so the speaker goes around the next piece

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
PE is physical education, a working out

explanation.surface: A scheming kind of speaker talking about exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working out' reads as solving something, but it is gym exercise, physical education; 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth operator is a shrewd, manipulative person who gets their way.

clue.text: Thin crisp food proposed for Nellie?

definitions.text: Thin crisp food proposed for Nellie?

parts.words: Thin crisp food proposed for Nellie?
parts.note: a crisp thin slice of bread also reads as a drink-raising salute offered to the soprano Dame Nellie

explanation.surface: Raising a glass to a famous singer with a crunchy snack.
explanation.walkthrough: The opera singer Dame Nellie Melba gave her name to this toast; a toast is also what one proposes in someone's honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Melba toast is very thin, dry, crisp toasted bread.

clue.text: Drink queen had with special tonic water abroad

indicators.note: special implies a specially altered version, so the letters of tonic are rearranged

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen
eau is the French word for water

explanation.surface: The queen took some special tonic water while overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges TONIC into COINT; 'had with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange-flavoured liqueur, a drink.

clue.text: Put in grave situation, six partners gathered for formal meeting

parts.note: to inter is to bury, putting someone in a grave
VI is six in Roman numerals
East and West are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Six people gather in a grave crisis for a formal meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, East and West play as partners, so EW; 'gathered' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An interview is a formal meeting to question or assess someone.

clue.text: Medal initially announced for director

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the initials are said aloud and spelt as they sound

parts.note: MC, the Military Cross, is a medal known by its initials

explanation.surface: A medal winner is announced by the person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Military Cross is a British gallantry medal, abbreviated MC; spelt out as said, it gives the word for a master of ceremonies.
explanation.definitionFit: An emcee directs proceedings at an event as master of ceremonies.

clue.text: Length that's determined by scanning

definitions.meaning: a unit of length in the metric system
scanning verse means working out its rhythm, the pattern of stressed syllables

explanation.surface: A distance measured by some scanning device.
explanation.definitionFit: A metre is both a unit of length and the rhythmic pattern of poetry revealed by scansion.

clue.text: Introductory parts of discontinued radio broadcast

parts.note: ex means former, no longer current

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of radio are rearranged

explanation.surface: Opening sections of a radio programme that has been axed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontinued radio' reads as a station taken off air, but 'discontinued' stands alone for former, and 'broadcast' scrambles radio (ORDIA).
explanation.definitionFit: Exordia, plural of exordium, are the introductory parts of speeches or treatises.

clue.text: Actors' good luck leading to member being in cast?

definitions.meaning: a theatrical wish of good luck, since saying good luck itself is thought unlucky

definitions.text: leading to member being in cast?
definitions.meaning: a fractured limb ends up in a plaster cast

explanation.surface: A good-luck wish for actors that ends up with someone in plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the actors of the first half but is a plaster cast; 'member' is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Break a leg is the actors' traditional wish for a good performance, and breaking a leg literally puts a limb in plaster.

clue.text: So-called expert giving king no problem in the long run

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
marathon runners speak of hitting the wall, sudden exhaustion

explanation.surface: An expert advises the king that nothing will go wrong in the long term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the long run' looks like 'eventually' but means a marathon, where runners hit the wall; 'giving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all is someone who claims to know everything, a self-styled expert.

clue.text: Dry wines found in facilities for travellers

parts.note: to air is to dry out, as with laundry
ports are fortified wines from Portugal

explanation.surface: Dry wines sold in airport lounges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Airports are the facilities where air travellers depart and arrive.

clue.text: Movin' up and down repeatedly in reel

definitions.meaning: bobbing about, with the final g dropped in the colloquial way
a spool on which thread is wound

explanation.surface: Someone dancing and bouncing about in a Scottish reel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reel' looks like the dance but is a spool; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobbin is a reel or spool for thread, and bobbin' is a dropped-g spelling of bobbing.

clue.text: Friend's purchase securing 1000 in two instalments

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the purchase holds the next piece

parts.note: a buy is a purchase, as in a good buy
D is 500 in Roman numerals, so two Ds make 1000

explanation.surface: A friend's purchase, paid for with 1000 spread over two payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friend's' is Friend is, a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A buddy is a close friend or pal.

clue.text: Wine and dine a lot, from what we hear

indicators.note: this phrase signals that the word for lot is heard and spelt as a word sounding the same

parts.note: one's lot in life is one's fate

explanation.surface: Someone does a lot of wining and dining, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: To fete someone is to honour them lavishly, typically with food and drink.

clue.text: I struggled with a climber on outside of building

definitions.text: with a climber on outside of building

parts.note: vied means competed or struggled

explanation.surface: Someone recalls struggling as a climber on the outside of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' looks like a mountaineer but is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivied describes walls covered with ivy, a climbing plant.

clue.text: Name of Pope, in either order

definitions.text: Name of Pope, in either order

parts.words: Name of Pope, in either order
parts.note: the poet's first name, which is also a papal name when placed after the title

explanation.surface: A question about a pontiff's name.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet Alexander Pope reverses to Pope Alexander, a name taken by several popes.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander was the first name of the poet Pope and also a papal name.

clue.text: Part of Spain from which one's exported port for England

indicators.note: exported means sent out, so the letter for one is removed

parts.note: New Castile is a historic region of central Spain
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Shipping goods from a Spanish region to an English port.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing I from NEW CASTILE leaves the English port.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcastle upon Tyne is a major port in north-east England.

clue.text: Not perfidious, like a monarch changing side at the front

indicators.note: R for right becomes L for left at the start of the word

parts.note: royal means befitting a king or queen

explanation.surface: A faithful subject, like the king, switches allegiance at the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyal means faithful, the opposite of perfidious or treacherous.
